Author: D. McClanahan et al.

Report_ID: Incident atopic dermatitis cumulative to 12 months
Title: A randomized trial of a barrier lipid replacement strategy for the prevention of atopic dermatitis and allergic sensitization: the PEBBLES pilot study
Author: Lowe et al.
Comment: The eligible cumulative 12-month analysis included 74 of 80 recruited infants (36 control and 38 cream). The reported risk ratio is nonsignificant and is oriented as cream versus control; no unreported effect transformation was calculated.
Design Type: Randomized, parallel, single-blind (outcome-assessor), controlled pilot trial
Study Environment: Term infants recruited from maternity wards with blinded clinical follow-up at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months
Content length: Twice daily from within the first 3 weeks of life through 6 months
Topic of Content: Prophylactic skin-barrier enhancement to prevent atopic dermatitis
Participant type: Term infants with a family history of allergic disease
Outcome measurement: U.K. working party definition; cumulative responses combined from prior clinical assessments
Outcome variable: Incident atopic dermatitis cumulative to 12 months

Report_ID: Diagnosis of eczema at age 2 years according to UK working party diagnostic criteria
Title: Daily emollient during infancy for prevention of eczema: the BEEP randomised controlled trial
Author: Chalmers et al.
Comment: The reported adjusted risk difference is −1.2% (95% CI −5.9 to 3.6), but this schema has no dedicated risk-difference CI fields; the point estimate is stored in effect_size_value. Values are retained in the paper's own emollient-versus-control direction and are not sign-reversed to impose the synthesis plan's positive-favors-intervention convention.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Emollient plus best-practice skin-care advice') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Multicentre pragmatic two-arm parallel-group randomized controlled trial
domain: Primary prevention of infant eczema (atopic dermatitis)
Study Environment: 12 hospitals and four primary care sites; follow-up usually in the family home
Medium: Daily whole-body topical emollient (Diprobase cream or Doublebase gel)
Content length: Daily from shortly after birth until age 1 year
Topic of Content: Skin-barrier enhancement and best-practice infant skin care
Participant type: Term newborn infants at high risk of eczema due to family history of atopic disease
Recruitment source: Antenatal or postnatal services, general-practitioner invitation letters, and hospital/community posters
Outcome measurement: Eczema over the past year defined by UK Working Party refinement of Hanifin and Rajka diagnostic criteria, assessed by masked research nurses at age 2 years
Outcome variable: Diagnosis of eczema at age 2 years according to UK working party diagnostic criteria
